## Goal

Notebook 04 learned one network with MIIC: 1,000 sender cells (CD8αα(I) and NK, 500 each), 635 receiver cells (DC1
500, aDC1 135), 25 L–R pairs from Table S5 (28 gene–gene links) and four metadata variables per group (population,
donor, chemistry, stage). This notebook reads that network against the claim of Park *et al.* 2020 (Fig. 4D, fig. S26):

> "GNG4⁺CD8αα⁺ T(I) cells expressed XCL1, which may be involved in the recruitment of XCR1-expressing DC1 cells. […]
> XCL1 is expressed most highly by CD8αα⁺ T(I) cells and at a lower level by NK cells […] a potential relay of signals
> from CD8αα⁺ T(I) cells to recruit XCR1⁺ DC1 cells into the medulla, where these cells are activated and up-regulate
> CCR7."

The claim has three parts, examined in turn: **(1) who produces XCL1** (sections 2), **(2) XCR1 on DC1 and the
activation that follows** (section 3), and **(3) the other signals between the same cells** (section 4). Sections 5
and 6 check the design variables and the orientations; section 7 draws the network.

**How to read a CausalCCC network.** Within each group (senders, receivers), a link means that two variables remain
dependent whatever other variable of the group is conditioned on; its strength is `info_shifted` (the mutual
information, in bits × number of cells, minus a complexity cost). The L–R links between the groups are **given**, not
learned: the two genes are never measured in the same cell, so these links only connect the two networks. What can be
learned is therefore *what each ligand and each receptor depends on in its own cells*.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

root <- getwd()
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))) {
  if (dirname(root) == root) stop("Repository root not found.")
  root <- dirname(root)
}
# link_name(), neighbors_of(), graph_distance(), column_cell_type(), network_data(), plot_network_*()
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))

res_dir   <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_case2_xcl1")
files_dir <- file.path(res_dir, "04_causalccc", "causalccc_files")
out_dir   <- file.path(res_dir, "05_interpretation")
fig_dir   <- file.path(root, "results", "figures", "thymus_case2_xcl1")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

miic_result <- readRDS(file.path(res_dir, "04_causalccc", "miic_input", "miic_result.rds"))
mosaic      <- read_csv(file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_df.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = Inf)
lr          <- read_tsv(file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_interactEdges.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

SEND <- "CD8αα(I)/NK"
RECV <- "DC1/aDC1"
META <- c("population", "donor", "method", "stage")

# Cell type of each variable: the group whose rows hold its values
row_type <- if_else(!is.na(mosaic$population_senders), SEND, RECV)
type_of  <- column_cell_type(mosaic, row_type)

# One row per pair of variables (MIIC lists each given L-R link twice, once per direction; notebook 04)
lr_links <- link_name(lr$ligands, lr$receptors)
edges <- miic_result$all.edges.summary |>
  filter(type == "P") |>
  distinct(pair_a = pmin(x, y), pair_b = pmax(x, y), .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-pair_a, -pair_b) |>
  mutate(is_lr = link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links,
         where = case_when(is_lr ~ "L–R (given)", type_of[x] == SEND ~ "within senders", .default = "within receivers"))
intracellular <- edges |> filter(!is_lr)

# Labels for the tables and drawings: no group suffix, metadata in brackets
var_label <- function(v) {
  label <- str_remove(v, "_(senders|receivers)$")
  if_else(label %in% META, paste0("[", label, "]"), label)
}
# Neighbours of a variable, strongest first, as one string: "gene (strength)"
neighbour_string <- function(v, n = Inf) {
  nb <- intracellular |> filter(x == v | y == v) |>
    transmute(other = if_else(x == v, y, x), info_shifted) |> arrange(desc(info_shifted)) |> head(n)
  if (nrow(nb) == 0) return("–")
  paste0(var_label(nb$other), " (", round(nb$info_shifted), ")", collapse = ", ")
}
degree_of <- function(v) map_int(v, \(g) sum(intracellular$x == g | intracellular$y == g))
```

## 1. Overview of the network

```{r}
#| label: overview

variables <- tibble(variable = names(mosaic), group = type_of[names(mosaic)],
                    kind = if_else(str_remove(names(mosaic), "_(senders|receivers)$") %in% META, "metadata", "gene"))
linked <- unique(c(edges$x, edges$y))

left_join(
  variables |> group_by(group) |>
    summarise(genes = sum(kind == "gene"), metadata = sum(kind == "metadata"),
              variables_linked = sum(variable %in% linked)) |>
    mutate(where = paste("within", if_else(group == SEND, "senders", "receivers"))),
  edges |> group_by(where) |>
    summarise(links = n(), oriented = sum(abs(infOrt) == 2), genuine_causations = sum(is_causal == "Y")),
  by = "where") |>
  bind_rows(edges |> filter(is_lr) |> summarise(where = "L–R (given)", links = n(), oriented = sum(abs(infOrt) == 2),
                                                genuine_causations = sum(is_causal == "Y"))) |>
  select(where, genes, metadata, variables_linked, links, oriented, genuine_causations)
```

**Hubs**: the variables with the most learned links in each group.

```{r}
#| label: hubs

degrees <- tibble(variable = unique(c(intracellular$x, intracellular$y))) |>
  mutate(group = type_of[variable], degree = degree_of(variable))
degrees |>
  group_by(group) |> slice_max(degree, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), label = paste0(var_label(variable), " (", degree, ")")) |>
  select(group, rank, label) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = label)
```

**Strongest learned links** in each group.

```{r}
#| label: strongest

intracellular |>
  group_by(where) |> slice_max(info_shifted, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(where, link = paste(var_label(x), "—", var_label(y)), strength = round(info_shifted)) |>
  ungroup()
```

**Reading.**
- Each group holds about 140 genes plus its 4 metadata variables, all of them linked. MIIC kept 293 links among the
  senders and 292 among the receivers, of which about one in ten is oriented and 9 are genuine causations in total.
- **Senders:** the two hubs are NKG7 and `[population]` (25 links each): the network is organised around the NK versus
  CD8αα(I) identity. The other hubs are housekeeping and glycolysis genes (GAPDH, ACTB, SERF2, PPIA, EEF1A1, TPT1,
  PTMA). Ribosomal genes were excluded from the gene selection (notebook 04), but these other highly expressed genes
  still share a lot of information with many pivots.
- **Receivers:** the hubs are CD74 and the MHC class II genes (antigen presentation), CPVL and LYZ (DC1 identity), and
  LAMP3 and `[population]` (activation, section 3).
- **Strongest links:** in both groups, the strongest link is `[donor]`–`[stage]`. Stage is fully determined by donor
  (section 5), so this link carries no biology. Next come NK identity (NKG7–`[population]`, TYROBP, FCER1G) among the
  senders, and the HLA class I and class II modules among the receivers.

## 2. Senders: what XCL1 depends on

```{r}
#| label: xcl-neighbours

tibble(variable = c("XCL1", "XCL2", "population_senders"),
       degree = degree_of(variable),
       neighbours = map_chr(variable, neighbour_string))
```

The network says that, once the NK / CD8αα(I) label is known, XCL1 no longer depends on stage, donor or chemistry.
This can be checked directly in the mosaic table (raw counts of the 1,000 sender cells):

```{r}
#| label: xcl-by-population-stage

mosaic |>
  filter(row_type == SEND) |>
  group_by(population = population_senders, stage = stage_senders) |>
  summarise(cells = n(), XCL1_detected = mean(XCL1 > 0), XCL1_mean = mean(XCL1),
            XCL2_detected = mean(XCL2 > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, c("early", "middle", "late"))) |>
  arrange(population, stage) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(v) round(v, 2)))
```

```{r}
#| label: xcl1-co-expression

# Co-expression of XCL1 with XCL2 and with the NK marker NKG7, per sender population
mosaic |>
  filter(row_type == SEND) |>
  group_by(population = population_senders) |>
  summarise(cells = n(),
            `XCL1+ among XCL2+` = mean(XCL1[XCL2 > 0] > 0),
            `XCL1+ among XCL2-` = mean(XCL1[XCL2 == 0] > 0),
            `NKG7 detected` = mean(NKG7 > 0)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(v) round(v, 2)))
```

**Reading.**
- **XCL1 has only two learned neighbours:** XCL2 (146) and `[population]` (49). So in these cells, XCL1 depends on
  which population the cell belongs to and on XCL2, and on nothing else among the ~140 sender variables. XCL2 is
  attached to the NK program (NKG7, 215) and to CRTAM.
- **NK cells are the main XCL1 source in this run:** 61–79% of NK cells express it, against 10–36% of CD8αα(I) cells.
  This agrees with notebook 01: CD8αα(I) leads only on the level within expressing cells.
- **In CD8αα(I), XCL1 is carried by a small XCL2⁺ subset:** 96% of XCL2⁺ CD8αα(I) cells express XCL1, against 9% of
  the others. Since only 3% of CD8αα(I) cells express NKG7, this subset is not contaminating NK cells. Whether it is
  the GNG4⁺ subset named in the paper is not tested here.
- **XCL1 in CD8αα(I) falls with age**, from 36% of cells (mean 19 counts) at 7–11 PCW to 10% (mean 1.8) postnatally
  from 15 months. In NK cells it goes the other way (61% → 79% → 73%). Yet the network shows **no XCL1–stage (or
  donor) link**. MIIC tests each dependence on the whole sender group, where these opposite trends probably blur
  each other. This is a limit of pooling the two populations, not evidence that XCL1 is stable with age: in CD8αα(I)
  cells, the claimed XCL1 source is mainly a fetal feature.

## 3. Receivers: XCR1, CCR7 and the activation of DC1

```{r}
#| label: receiver-neighbours

recv_genes <- c("XCR1", "CCR7", "LAMP3", "CD40", "CD80", "CD86", "IL12B", "population_receivers")
tibble(variable = recv_genes, degree = degree_of(variable), neighbours = map_chr(variable, neighbour_string))
```

```{r}
#| label: receiver-distances

# Number of learned links between XCR1 and the activation genes (within the receivers)
d <- graph_distance(intracellular |> filter(where == "within receivers"), "XCR1")
tibble(from = "XCR1", to = c("population_receivers", "FGL2", "CCR7", "LAMP3", "CD40", "CD80", "CD86", "IL12B", "CD83"),
       links_away = unname(d[to]))
```

In the mosaic table, XCR1 and CCR7 are almost mutually exclusive, and both are explained by the DC1 / aDC1 label:

```{r}
#| label: xcr1-ccr7

mosaic |>
  filter(row_type == RECV) |>
  mutate(XCR1 = if_else(XCR1 > 0, "XCR1+", "XCR1-"), CCR7 = if_else(CCR7 > 0, "CCR7+", "CCR7-")) |>
  count(population = population_receivers, XCR1, CCR7) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(XCR1, CCR7), values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

**Reading.**
- **XCR1 has two learned neighbours:** FGL2 (76), a DC1 gene, and `[population]` (16). Within the receivers, it does not
  depend on any activation gene.
- **CCR7 and LAMP3 are attached to `[population]`** (219 and 199) and to the activation program of mature DCs: CCR7 to
  CD83, BIRC3 and SAMSN1; LAMP3 to EBI3, FSCN1, LAD1, CD40, CD80, IL12B, TRAF1 and IL4I1. XCR1 is two links away
  from CCR7 and LAMP3, and only through the DC1 / aDC1 label; it is three links from CD40, CD80, CD83 and IL12B.
- **XCR1 and CCR7 are almost mutually exclusive:**
  - DC1: 280 of 500 cells express XCR1 and only 20 express CCR7 (10 express both);
  - aDC1: 121 of 135 express CCR7 and only 3 express XCR1.

  **Activation is therefore a switch from an XCR1⁺ state to a CCR7⁺ state.**
- **What this supports and what it doesn't:** it fits the second half of the claim ("activated […] up-regulate CCR7")
  as a change of cell state. It gives no evidence that XCL1–XCR1 signalling *causes* this activation: within the
  receivers, the activation program does not depend on how much XCR1 a cell expresses, and activated cells have
  lost XCR1. The recruitment "into the medulla" is a spatial statement, which dissociated single-cell data cannot test.

## 4. The other L–R links

For every given link, the learned context of the ligand (in the senders) and of the receptor (in the receivers). A
ligand or receptor linked to `[population]` is specific to one of the two populations of its group; a variable with no
learned link has no detectable dependence on anything else in the network.

```{r}
#| label: lr-table

lr_table <- lr |>
  mutate(ligand = var_label(ligands), receptor = var_label(receptors),
         ligand_degree = degree_of(ligands), receptor_degree = degree_of(receptors),
         ligand_to_population = map_lgl(ligands, \(g) "population_senders" %in% neighbors_of(g, intracellular)$neighbor),
         receptor_to_population = map_lgl(receptors, \(g) "population_receivers" %in% neighbors_of(g, intracellular)$neighbor),
         ligand_neighbours = map_chr(ligands, neighbour_string, n = 4),
         receptor_neighbours = map_chr(receptors, neighbour_string, n = 4))
lr_table |>
  select(ligand, receptor, ligand_degree, ligand_to_population, receptor_degree, receptor_to_population,
         ligand_neighbours, receptor_neighbours) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
#| label: lr-classes

lr_table |>
  mutate(ligand_side = case_when(ligand_degree == 0 ~ "isolated",
                                 ligand_to_population ~ "population-specific",
                                 .default = "linked, not to population"),
         receptor_side = case_when(receptor_degree == 0 ~ "isolated",
                                   receptor_to_population ~ "population-specific",
                                   .default = "linked, not to population")) |>
  count(ligand_side, receptor_side)
```

**Reading.**
- **Overview of the 28 links:**
  - for 15, neither side is tied to the population label;
  - for 9, only the ligand is population-specific;
  - for 2, only the receptor is;
  - for 2, **both sides are: XCL1 → XCR1 and PDCD1 → CD274**. These are the two pairs whose ligand marks one sender
    population and whose receptor marks one receiver state.
- **Costimulation reaches the activation program, XCR1 does not.**
  - The receptors CD40 and CD80 are direct neighbours of LAMP3, and CD274 (PD-L1) is tied to the aDC1 label.
  - Their ligands belong to the T-cell module of the senders: CD28 is tied to `[population]` (CD8αα(I) cells), and
    CD40LG is linked to CD28, ITM2A and CD200.
  - So the classical T cell–DC pairs CD40LG → CD40, CD28 → CD80 / CD86 and PDCD1 → CD274 connect CD8αα(I) cells to
    the activated DC1 state more directly than XCL1 → XCR1 does.
  - Caveat: CD40, CD80 and CD274 are themselves activation markers, so these links reflect co-expression in aDC1 and
    do not prove signalling.
- **CRTAM → CADM1 parallels the XCL axis.** CRTAM is linked to XCL2 (52), and CADM1 to CLEC9A (150), the DC1 marker.
  CRTAM–CADM1 is a known recognition pair between XCL1-producing cytotoxic cells and cross-presenting DC1, so it
  points to the same cells as XCL1 → XCR1.
- **NK-specific ligands:** IFNG, KLRF1, TIGIT and TNFSF14 are tied to the population label (NK cells). Their receptors
  are not specific to DC1 or aDC1.
- **Ubiquitous pairs:** MIF and APP → CD74 again rank first in S5 (as in thymus case 1), but the network places MIF in
  a housekeeping and glycolysis module (GAPDH, GPI, PSMA6) and CD74 in the MHC class II module (HLA-DPA1, HLA-DRB5).
  Nothing in the network is specific to these pairs.
- **Adhesion pairs:** the integrin and adhesion pairs (LFA-1 / ICAM1, VLA-4 / PLAUR, SELL / SELPLG, SPN / ICAM1) sit
  mostly among cytoskeletal and housekeeping genes. On the receiver side, ICAM1 is linked to NF-κB target genes (SRGN,
  NFKBIA, BCL2A1).

## 5. Design variables: donor, stage, chemistry

```{r}
#| label: stage-donor

# Each donor has a single age, so stage is a function of donor
mosaic |>
  filter(row_type == SEND) |>
  distinct(donor = donor_senders, stage = stage_senders) |>
  count(donor) |>
  summarise(donors = n(), donors_with_one_stage = sum(n == 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: meta-neighbours

tibble(variable = c("donor_senders", "stage_senders", "method_senders",
                    "donor_receivers", "stage_receivers", "method_receivers"),
       degree = degree_of(variable), neighbours = map_chr(variable, neighbour_string))
```

```{r}
#| label: claim-to-meta

# Distance from the genes of the claim to the design variables (learned links only)
map(c("XCL1", "XCL2", "XCR1", "CCR7"), \(g) {
  d <- graph_distance(intracellular, g)
  side <- if_else(type_of[g] == SEND, "senders", "receivers")
  tibble(gene = g, donor = d[paste0("donor_", side)], stage = d[paste0("stage_", side)],
         chemistry = d[paste0("method_", side)])
}) |> list_rbind()
```

**Reading.**
- **Stage carries no information beyond donor:** each of the 22 donors of the sender group has a single stage, so
  `[stage]` links only to `[donor]`. Stage is therefore redundant as a network variable.
- **Donor** links to a few genes in each group:
  - senders: NKG7 (the share of NK cells differs between donors) and some housekeeping genes;
  - receivers: HLA-DRB5 and HLA-DQA2. These depend on the donor's HLA haplotype (HLA-DRB5 exists only on DR51-group
    haplotypes, DR15/DR16), and MIIC orients donor → HLA-DRB5 as a genuine causation, a sensible result.
- **Chemistry (3′ / 5′)** links to a handful of genes (PTPRCAP, GABARAP, YWHAZ, NME2, ATP6V0C, TMSB4X), a technical
  effect.
- **The claim's genes are 2 to 5 links away from donor, stage and chemistry.** So the XCL1, XCL2, XCR1 and CCR7
  results above are not direct effects of donor or technology.

## 6. Orientations and genuine causations

MIIC orients a link when the data contain a v-structure (two variables that are independent but become dependent
once a third is known). A "genuine causation" (`is_causal` = Y) is an orientation that cannot be explained by a hidden
common cause. Orientations into or out of a metadata variable (a cell label, a donor) are not causal statements about
biology: they only record which variables are independent of each other.

```{r}
#| label: orientations

oriented <- edges |>
  filter(abs(infOrt) == 2) |>
  transmute(from = if_else(infOrt == 2, x, y), to = if_else(infOrt == 2, y, x), where,
            strength = round(info_shifted), genuine = is_causal,
            involves_metadata = str_detect(paste(from, to), "(population|donor|method|stage)_"))
oriented |> count(where, involves_metadata, genuine)
```

```{r}
#| label: genuine

oriented |>
  filter(genuine == "Y" | str_detect(paste(from, to), "XCL|XCR1|CCR7|LAMP3")) |>
  mutate(from = var_label(from), to = var_label(to)) |>
  arrange(desc(genuine), desc(strength)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

**Reading.**
- 65 links are oriented: 35 among the senders and 30 among the receivers.
- **Genuine causations:** there are 9.
  - 7 are between genes: UBA52 → TMSB4X, NKG7 → IL2RB, GAPDH → TPI1, SERF2 → FAU, GAPDH → COX6C, LYZ → ITGB2 and
    NKG7 → ARPC5L. These are housekeeping, glycolysis or cell-identity genes, with no clear signalling meaning.
  - 2 involve metadata: `[population]` → NUCB2 and `[donor]` → HLA-DRB5 (section 5).
- **None involves XCL1, XCL2, XCR1 or CCR7.**
- **The arrow XCL1 → `[population]` is not causal:** it is a v-structure. XCL1, CD28 and other population-specific
  genes are independent of each other but each depends on the label, so MIIC points them into it.

## 7. The network, drawn

How to read the drawings: colours are the two groups; diamonds are the centres (XCL1, XCL2, XCR1); dashed lines are the
given L–R links (drawn thin, since their strength is set by CausalCCC); an arrowhead is an orientation found by MIIC,
and a green link a genuine causation; thicker links are stronger. Metadata variables are in brackets.

```{r}
#| label: drawing-setup

# Colours of the two groups for the drawing functions of scripts/helpers.R (which read these two global vectors)
cell_type_colours <- set_names(c("#f2c57c", "#9cc3e6"), c(SEND, RECV))
cell_type_borders <- set_names(c("#a8742a", "#2f6491"), c(SEND, RECV))
centres <- c("XCL1", "XCL2", "XCR1")
claim_net <- network_data(edges, lr_links, type_of, var_label, centres = centres, max_distance = 2)
c(variables = nrow(claim_net$nodes), links = nrow(claim_net$links))
```

### The neighbourhood of the claim

All variables at most two learned links away from XCL1, XCL2 or XCR1, and the links among them. Interactive: hover
over a node or a link for details, click a node to highlight its neighbours, drag to rearrange, scroll to zoom.

```{r}
#| label: fig-claim-interactive

plot_network_interactive(claim_net, title = "XCL1 / XCL2 → XCR1: second-degree neighbourhood", height = "750px")
```

The same neighbourhood as a static figure (also saved to `results/figures/thymus_case2_xcl1/05_claim_neighbourhood.png`):

```{r}
#| label: fig-claim-static
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 9

p <- plot_network_static(claim_net, title = "XCL1 / XCL2 → XCR1: second-degree neighbourhood", label_size = 2.8)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "05_claim_neighbourhood.png"), p, width = 11, height = 9, dpi = 200)
p
```

### The whole network

All 613 links. With about 285 variables the drawing is dense: zoom in, or click a gene to highlight its neighbours.

```{r}
#| label: fig-full

network_data(edges, lr_links, type_of, var_label) |>
  plot_network_interactive(title = "CD8αα(I)/NK → DC1/aDC1: all links", height = "850px")
```

```{r}
#| label: export

# Retained links with their group and labels, for later notebooks
edges |>
  transmute(x, y, x_label = var_label(x), y_label = var_label(y), where, is_lr, info_shifted, infOrt, is_causal) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "retained_links.csv"))
lr_table |> select(-ligands, -receptors) |> write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "lr_links_context.csv"))
list.files(out_dir)
```

## Conclusions

The claim has three parts; the network supports them unevenly.

1. **"GNG4⁺ CD8αα⁺ T(I) cells express XCL1, most highly […], and NK cells at a lower level": partly supported.**
   XCL1 depends only on XCL2 and on the population label. In this run, NK cells are the main source (61–79% of cells
   against 10–36%). In CD8αα(I) cells, XCL1 is carried by a small XCL1⁺XCL2⁺ subset whose share falls from fetal (36%)
   to postnatal (10%) thymus. "Most highly" holds only for the level within expressing cells (notebook 01).
2. **"Recruitment of XCR1⁺ DC1, which are then activated and up-regulate CCR7": consistent as a change of state, not
   shown as a consequence.** XCR1 marks resting DC1 and CCR7 / LAMP3 mark activated DC1; the two states are almost
   mutually exclusive and are connected only through the DC1 / aDC1 label. Nothing in the receivers' network makes the
   activation program depend on XCR1, and recruitment into the medulla cannot be tested on dissociated cells.
3. **Other signals between the same cells.**
   - The costimulation pairs from CD8αα(I) cells (CD40LG → CD40, CD28 → CD80 / CD86, PDCD1 → CD274) reach the
     activation program of aDC1 more directly than XCL1 → XCR1.
   - CRTAM → CADM1 links the XCL2⁺ cytotoxic program to CLEC9A⁺ DC1, in parallel with the XCL axis.
   - The top-ranked S5 pairs (MIF / APP → CD74) are not specific to these cells.

**Technical checks.**
- Donor and chemistry do not touch the claim's genes directly.
- Stage is redundant with donor.
- Pooling NK and CD8αα(I) cells hides the age decline of XCL1 in CD8αα(I), because NK cells go the opposite way.

**Possible next steps.**
- A run with CD8αα(I) senders only, fetal versus postnatal, to test the age dependence of XCL1 directly.
- A check of GNG4 in the XCL1⁺ CD8αα(I) subset.
- The same analysis on the authors' T-cell object (finer annotation), which fig. S26 was drawn from.

**Outputs:**
- `results/thymus_case2_xcl1/05_interpretation/retained_links.csv`: every link, with group and labels;
- `results/thymus_case2_xcl1/05_interpretation/lr_links_context.csv`: the context of each L–R link;
- `results/figures/thymus_case2_xcl1/05_claim_neighbourhood.png`: the static figure.
